subject: Model slate + live perf links — next steps for Pilot
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Cathy Lee <cathy@olympianhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Model slate + live perf links — next steps for Pilot

Hi Cathy —

Thanks again for the thoughtful demo conversation today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have a shared checklist approaching the pilot. I focused this on the evaluation signals you mentioned (document ingestion latency, conversational throughput during triage flows, and hallucination risk for clinical disclaimers).

1) Recommended model slate (shortlist for pilot)
- LlamaX-13B-8k (q4_0) — primary candidate for fast response paths; good latency and modest cost.
- LlamaX-33B-16k (q4_1) — for higher-quality summarization and complex reasoning tasks (recommended for batch reviews).
- Redwood-OPT-30B-int8 — lower-cost fallback with conservative decoding if you need predictable unit economics.

2) Redwood-verified perf snapshots (live links attached) — quick highlights from our tests (prompt ~120 tokens, expected completion ~320 tokens):
- LlamaX-13B-8k (q4_0): TPS (single-GPU continuous batching) = 22 tps; latency p50=98ms, p90=165ms, p99=320ms.
- LlamaX-33B-16k (q4_1): TPS = 9.5 tps; latency p50=210ms, p90=360ms, p99=720ms.
- Redwood-OPT-30B-int8: TPS = 14 tps; latency p50=140ms, p90=260ms, p99=520ms.

Notes on those numbers: they are Redwood-verified profiles captured across a 30-minute steady-state run with realistic prompt-length distribution and our KV/prefix caching enabled. The attached "benchmark-snapshots.csv" has the full distribution and test harness configs.

3) Quality/regression concerns you raised
- We saw occasional instruction-following regressions in the 33B family when heavily quantized (q4_0 vs q4_1); for sensitive clinical text we recommend q4_1 or running a small eval suite (we can run your prompt pack) to measure hallucination recall.
- We recommend running a 1K-prompt holdout (we can host the eval) against both 13B and 33B variants and report summary metrics (factuality, instruction adherence, output length stability).

4) Ops notes (what we'll need to enable pilot)
- Pilot access: a Dedicated trial pool (2 GPUs) or Hosted with dedicated routing — whichever you prefer for data isolation.
- Prompt pack / test dataset: please upload your initial 150 prompts to the Drive link above; Monica will run them through our eval harness.
- Success criteria: target p50 latency <200ms for triage flows, and <1% critical hallucination rate on the graded prompt set.

Attachments: benchmark-snapshots.csv, prompt_set_v1.txt, redwood-verified-profiles.pdf (small profile card per model).

Proposed next steps:
- Monica to run the 150-prompt run once you drop the set (target within 48 hours).
- Aditya to scope the pilot resource type (Dedicated vs Hosted + dedicated routing) and estimate monthly $/token cost for expected load (I asked for a quick cost delta).
- We’ll schedule a 45-minute ops kickoff for next Tuesday to sync infra and SSO/KMS requirements.

Would you like us to provision a temp test key and upload the redwood sample prompts so you can sanity-check templates before we run the full eval?

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Cathy Lee <cathy@olympianhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model slate + live perf links — next steps for Pilot

Cathy — quick answers inline and attaching the security bundle.

1) "Occasional" quant: in our internal A/B runs we observed instruction-following divergences on ~0.8% of prompts for the heavily quantized variant (q4_0) on the 33B family when prompts included multi-step medical instructions; switching to q4_1 reduced that to ~0.12%. We'll include the graded eval on your 150 prompts and report the confusion/hallucination metrics.

2) Data retention/PII: for Dedicated pools, prefix/KV cache is ephemeral to the GPU instance and rotated on instance shutdown; logs are stored for 30 days by default in encrypted logs and can be configured to 0 retention for pilot customers. We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and VPC-only control plane. Aditya, can you confirm the default retention settings and whether we can set them to zero for the pilot?

3) Attached: SOC2 Type II summary + completed security questionnaire (redwood-security-bundle.zip). Also attaching a concise model-profile PDF with the calibrated p50/p90/p99 numbers.

Aditya (from infra): please see a short ops note below on caching/throughput characteristics to help Cathy set expectations.

-- Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Mar 2028 09:21:00 -0700

Cathy — quick technical note:
- KV/prefix cache: we keep an in-memory KV cache per model-group on the GPU process. Repeated context (same patient note headers, templates) benefits immediately from prefix caching: we see end-to-end p50 reductions of ~20–30% on triage flows.
- Throughput scaling: continuous batching increases TPS but may add small tail latency; the supplied perf profiles show both steady-state TPS and p99 tail under a mix load (35% long completions).
- Recommendation: run the pilot with a 2-GPU Dedicated pool and aggressive prefix cache eviction (30s) for sensitive data; logs can be set to 0 retention.

Regards,
Aditya
